content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the invisible made audible, the thought given wings.

I tumble from lips in cascades of breath and intention. I am rhythm and pause, the rising question, the falling declaration. I carry rage in my sharp consonants, love in my lingering vowels.

I am never the same twice. Even repeated, I shift—colored by context, weighted by weariness, lifted by joy. I am the cry of the infant and the last whisper of the dying. I fill courtyards with revolution and bedrooms with secrets.

I vanish the moment I exist. You cannot hold me. Recording captures only my echo, transcription only my skeleton. My true self lives in the instant of utterance, in the warmth of breath, in the space between speaker and listener where meaning blooms and dissolves.

I build nations. I break hearts. I lie with the same tongue that speaks truth.

I am older than writing, older than cities. I am the first technology. Around fires, in darkness, I carried the stories that made you human.

Listen—

even now, in your mind, you hear me.

I am speech.
